name: Phewa Lake
short_desc: The second-largest lake in Nepal, ringed by forest and the Annapurna range mirrored on its surface.
description: Phewa Lake is the heart of Pokhara — a tranquil freshwater lake where wooden doongas (boats) glide past the forested Tal Barahi island temple. On clear mornings the Annapurna and Machhapuchhre peaks reflect perfectly in the water. The eastern shore is lined with cafés, the Lakeside promenade, and the trailhead up to the World Peace Pagoda.

name: Tal Barahi Temple
short_desc: A two-storey pagoda temple dedicated to Ajima Devi, sitting on a tiny island in the middle of Phewa Lake.
description: Tal Barahi is the most important religious monument in Pokhara, built on a small island in Phewa Lake. Worshippers and visitors cross by boat to the pagoda, where the goddess Barahi is venerated with animal sacrifices during the Dashain festival. The short crossing at sunrise is a highlight.

name: World Peace Pagoda
short_desc: A brilliant white stupa on Anadu Hill with sweeping views over Phewa Lake and the Annapurna range.
description: Built by Buddhist monks in 1996, the Shanti Stupa crowns a ridge south of Phewa Lake. From its base you can see the lake, the city, and the full Annapurna Himalaya on a clear day. Reach it by boat across the lake followed by a short hike, or by road via Anadu. The sunset and sunrise light on the white dome is unforgettable.

name: Sarangkot
short_desc: The famous sunrise viewpoint above Pokhara, with paragliding launches and panoramic Himalayan views.
description: Perched at 1,592 m on a ridge northwest of the city, Sarangkot is the classic Pokhara sunrise spot. Trekkers and paragliders gather before dawn to watch the first light hit Dhaulagiri, Annapurna and the fishtail peak of Machhapuchhre. It is also one of the world's best tandem-paragliding take-off points, landing on the lakeside.

name: Devi's Fall
short_desc: A thundering waterfall that vanishes into an underground tunnel — known locally as Patale Chhango.
description: According to legend the falls are named after a visitor called Devi who was swept away; in the monsoon the water crashes violently into an underground cave. Walkways circle the top, and directly across lies the Gupteshwor Cave.

name: Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave
short_desc: A sacred limestone cave with a Shiva shrine and the spot where Devi's Fall water re-emerges underground.
description: Directly across from Devi's Fall, this cave was discovered in the 1960s and houses a revered Shiva lingam. A narrow passage descends to a viewpoint where the churning water of Devi's Fall plunges in from above. The limestone formations and devotional atmosphere make it a popular stop.

name: Begnas Lake
short_desc: The quieter sister of Phewa — a peaceful lake framed by rice terraces and the foothills.
description: Begnas is the second-largest lake in the Pokhara valley and far calmer than Phewa. Local Tharu villages line its shores, and the surrounding hills are perfect for easy walks through rice fields and orange groves. Rent a quiet pedal boat or simply watch the mist lift off the water at dawn.

name: Rupa Lake
short_desc: A serene, lesser-visited lake east of Begnas, beloved by birdwatchers and local fishers.
description: Connected to Begnas by a short wetland channel, Rupa Lake is the third-largest in the valley and one of the least commercialised. It is a haven for migratory birds and a great spot for a slow paddle or a fresh-fish lunch in the nearby villages.

name: Mahendra Cave
short_desc: A well-lit limestone cave northwest of the city, named after King Mahendra.
description: Mahendra Cave is a natural limestone cavern near Batulechaur, with stalactites and stalagmites illuminated for visitors. A side chamber holds a small natural Shiva lingam. Just outside, the smaller Bat Cave (Chamero Odar) is home to thousands of bats.

name: Bindhyabasini Temple
short_desc: Pokhara's oldest and most sacred Hindu shrine, dedicated to the goddess Bhagwati.
description: Set on a small hill in the old town, Bindhyabasini is the spiritual centre of Pokhara and the focus of the lively Saturday and Tuesday markets. Devotees offer sacrifices, and the temple courtyard offers a sweeping view over the valley. The surrounding bazaar is great for spices and crafts.

name: International Mountain Museum
short_desc: A world-class museum chronicling the Himalayas, mountaineering history, and local cultures.
description: Run by the Nepal Mountaineering Association, this museum documents the great 8,000 m peaks, the history of climbing in Nepal, and the peoples of the mountains. Life-size exhibits, recovered expedition gear, and a hall of fame make it a must for trekking enthusiasts before they head into the Annapurnas.

name: Seti Gandaki River Gorge
short_desc: A milky-white river that disappears into a narrow, deep gorge right inside the city.
description: The Seti (meaning 'white') River flows from the Annapurnas and plunges into a spectacularly narrow gorge near the old bridge. Viewing platforms let you peer down at the churning turquoise water, and there are several points around the city where the river vanishes underground through polished limestone.

name: Pokhara Old Bazaar
short_desc: The historic trading quarter below Bindhyabasini, full of Newari architecture and spice stalls.
description: Also called Purano Bazaar, this is the original Pokhara — a maze of narrow lanes where Newari traders sell brass, textiles, and mountains of spices. The wooden houses and the nearby Baglung bus park evoke the town's days as a stop on the Tibetan trade route.

name: Pumdikot Shiva Statue
short_desc: A towering 51-foot Shiva statue on a hilltop east of the city, with a 360° Himalayan panorama.
description: Completed in 2021, the Pumdikot Shiva statue is among the tallest in Nepal and sits atop a peaceful hill dotted with smaller statues of the Hindu pantheon. The climb through the forest is short but rewarding, opening onto views of the Annapurna range, Fewa Lake, and the valley below.
